pr_title: Fix scheduler cache inconsistency upon Pods with same name but different UIDs
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

(This PR is taken over from #85910 due to its inactive activity)

The root cause is from API server which may combine a Delete and Add Pod event (the same Pod name) as a Update event:

(copied from original issue)

> since PR(#61069), podKey in scheduler cache use pod's UID instead of namespace/name
however, the key in SharedIndexInformer still use namespace/name
in this upper case, delete the pod and create a same name pod may be delivered as one update notification.( see disscusion： #83810)

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #85726.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
In a HA env, during the period a standby scheduler lost connection to API server, if a Pod is deleted and recreated, and the standby scheduler becomes master afterwards, there could be a scheduler cache corruption. This PR fixes this issue. 
```

wow, you would think that events are per pod as identified by its UID! It is surprising to me that a delete followed by add are merged because those are two different pods!

> wow, you would think that events are per pod as identified by its UID! It is surprising to me that a delete followed by add are merged because those are two different pods!

If I understand https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83810#issuecomment-541885957 correctly, it's the case.

_Maybe_ for a continuous HTTP watch, it's still 2 events, otherwise in the reproduce steps above, testPod wouldn't be able to schedule to a node.
But for a suspended and continued HTTP watch (in the above example, it's schedB), it seems API server will replay from the last watched position, and send that "problematic" Update event.

issue_context.title: Deleted pods may remain in scheduler cache and cause scheduling exception
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
pod can't be removed from scheduler cache when be deleted,  logs in kube-scheduler is below:

I1128 16:41:50.819639   31593 leaderelection.go:344] lock is held by shaphicpra14907_64ccb0c5-aaa1-435d-a4b4-ead4bb3de63b and has not yet expired
I1128 16:41:50.819678   31593 leaderelection.go:240] failed to acquire lease kube-system/kube-scheduler
I1128 16:41:53.740234   31593 leaderelection.go:344] lock is held by shaphicpra14907_64ccb0c5-aaa1-435d-a4b4-ead4bb3de63b and has not yet expired
I1128 16:41:53.740365   31593 leaderelection.go:240] failed to acquire lease kube-system/kube-scheduler
I1128 16:41:57.734692   31593 leaderelection.go:245] successfully acquired lease kube-system/kube-scheduler
I1128 16:41:57.834958   31593 shared_informer.go:176] caches populated
E1128 16:42:11.731020   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
E1128 16:42:12.339189   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
E1128 16:42:12.345323   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
E1128 16:42:20.628894   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
E1128 16:42:20.632578   31593 eventhandlers.go:254] scheduler cache RemovePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not found in scheduler cache, so cannot be removed from it


**What you expected to happen**:

pod in scheduler cache can be deleted successfully when pod is deleted

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

main steps to reproduce this bug is these:
1. two scheduler run in leader-elect=true mode，schedulerA is the leader scheduler, and schedulerB is an assistant.
2. create pod1 with "namespace1/name1" and it runs on Node1
3. break down the network between schedulerB and kube-apiserver
4. delete pod1 and create pod2 with same name, ie "namespace1/name1" and pod2 been assigned to Node1 by schedulerA again.
5. turn off schedulerA and recover the network between schedulerB and kube-apiserver, and then schedulerB become the leader scheduler.
6. delete pod2. this time log in schedulerB will print this: 

E1128 16:42:11.731020   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
E1128 16:42:20.632578   31593 eventhandlers.go:254] scheduler cache RemovePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not found in scheduler cache, so cannot be removed from it

7. At this time, if I create a new pod3 with podAntiAffinity to pod1. the result is pod3 can't been assigned to Node1 because pod1 is still in schedulerB's scheduler cache.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

the reason of this bug is below:

since PR(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61069), podKey in scheduler cache use pod's UID instead of namespace/name
however, the key in SharedIndexInformer still use namespace/name
in this upper case, delete the pod and create a same name pod may be delivered as one update notification.( see disscusion： https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83810)
scheduler received pod update notification and then print below log.

E1128 16:42:11.731020   31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated

@Huang-Wei , fix for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83810 just resolved the case add event may be lost after deletion event. It doesn't solve the problem that  a delete followed by an add may be delivered as one update notification and it's thought normal from MikeSpreitzer's comment. The main cause of this problem is scheduler cache use Pod UID as key while sharedInformer use namespace/name. 
Still, I also test with the latest kubernetes code. The bug of this issue reappeared.

review_comments: Why are we here? shouldn't we be here only if NodeName was set? it is not going to be set for the new pod, right?

It's described in #85726 in a HA setup and the author provided a detailed log. Basically it's like this:

- schedA as the master, schedB as the standby.
- testPod is scheduled to node1; schedA and schedB both gets that cached properly.
- disconnect schedB lost connection to API server (schedB is still alive).
- at the same time, testPod is deleted and then created - schedA works fine - 2 events (Delete and Add) get received, and the new testPod got scheduled (to node1 let's say).
- shut down schedA and recover schedB's connection to API server.
- an interesting thing happens. schedB receives 1 Update event (instead of 2 events) on testPod. Because schedB only has the stale testPod's UID in place, and the internal scheduler `cache state` uses UID to check the Pod's presence, it throws an error and failed the update:
    ```
    E1128 16:42:11.731020 31593 eventhandlers.go:226] scheduler cache UpdatePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not added to scheduler cache, so cannot be updated
    ```
- this error is critical, as it means the stale testPod live in scheduler's cache (instead of the new testPod) is corrupted.
- deleting testPod doesn't help, as it cannot be deleted due to UID not found.
    ```
    E1128 16:42:20.632578 31593 eventhandlers.go:254] scheduler cache RemovePod failed: pod 3c6696c6-decb-4abd-a1d3-d891e032459d is not found in scheduler cache, so cannot be removed from it
    ```

ah, ok, so testPod did get scheduled a second time already, and so it's NodeName is set and that triggers a proper update.

I was assuming that the new pod isn't scheduled yet, and so according to the [OnUpdate handler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L264-L276) the update should change to a delete event on the cache and an add event on the queue, which make sense.
Is there a bug filled for kube-apiserver? I'm fine with dealing with it here for now.

> Is there a bug filled for kube-apiserver?

I _prefer_ to believe it's a bug, but seems it's not the case from api's perspective, and I don't it can be "fixed" b/c the underlying DeltaFIFO queue is using namespace/name as the index.
